UT-2026-HB134.policyArea: Board of Pardons and Parole, Bureau of Criminal Identification, Courts
UT-2026-HB134.aiSummary: The bill changes Utah rules for moving probation or parole supervision to another state under the interstate compact, which is the agreement states use to supervise offenders across state lines. It raises the transfer fee from $50 to $90, says a person must already be under state supervision before applying, and sets new steps for courts, the Board of Pardons and Parole, and the Bureau of Criminal Identification when arrest warrants are issued for people supervised in another state. It also tells the bureau to send those warrants to the National Crime Information Center and makes other reporting and code clean-up changes.

UT-2026-HB113.policyArea: Crimes, Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice, Public Safety
UT-2026-HB113.aiSummary: The bill would expand Utah’s crime of emergency reporting abuse to cover some 911 calls made when no real or perceived emergency, crime, or other public safety risk exists, if the person was already told that kind of report was not proper. It would also add tougher penalties, including required reimbursement of response costs and either at least four days in jail or at least 40 hours of community service. The bill takes effect on May 6, 2026, and it was signed into law.

UT-2026-SB201.policyArea: Animals, Governmental Nonprofit Corporations, Political Subdivisions (Local Issues)
UT-2026-SB201.aiSummary: This law changes how animal shelters in Utah can put down dogs and cats. It says a shelter may do so only after other choices, like adoption, transfer, or return to the owner, are not available, and after required notice and wait times. It also lets shelters skip notice to a rescue group in some cases, such as if the group has people tied to animal cruelty or neglect cases or is under a court order that blocks it from taking animals. It takes effect on May 6, 2026.

It would also let the Utah Energy Council give guidance and do early studies, and it would require both groups to report these activities in their yearly reports. The office could also pursue a Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campus and must study state laws and rules for barriers to hosting it. No money is set aside in the bill, and the changes take effect on 05/06/26.

UT-2026-HB323.aiSummary: Utah passed a law that sets up rules for testing and disposing of solar panel waste, starting new state oversight of how old panels are handled. It requires solar retailers to give customers more written notice about disposal, possible tests, and costs, and it lets the state require hazardous waste testing before disposal. UT-2026-HB209.aiSummary: This law changes Utah voting rules and adds a new system for checking whether a registered voter is a U.S. citizen. It also lets voters choose whether to show proof of U.S. citizenship when registering or before voting; if they do not show it, they may only vote in federal races. The law also changes voter forms, ballot cure steps, and voter list rules.
